Generality is honest and specific. The move is stated abstractly in 'When to use it': pointwise setoid equality built from order antisymmetry, two maps that reflect the order and preserve a dense subset (here the rationals), excluded middle in the codomain, and a statement symmetric under swapping the maps so wlog applies. This generalizes past the example (the dense subset is named as a parameter, 'here the rationals'). 'When not to use' names four concrete failure points that match the copied code: codomain only Real.structure not Real.model (reals_classic/ratR_dense live on the model's sup axioms / find_range1z), maps that do not reflect the order (Real.morph_le is the iff that pulls the gap back), intensional = instead of Real.eq (real.v:121 defines eq as le x y AND le y x), and asymmetric directions defeating wlog. Consequences restate the same obligations and failure modes consistently. Good-leaf question is answered explicitly (README lines 108-112): each child is a self-contained statement whose proof closes on its own or from named siblings and bottoms out in the model's axioms (reals_classic via real_sup_total, ratR_dense via find_range1z, Rmorph_rat via phiM/Rmorph_inv/Rmorph_int), which I confirmed by reading the cited line ranges. Minor non-blocking note: the consequences parenthetical attributes the step '~(phi x <= psi x) is psi x < phi x' to totality, but that is definitional (real.v:212 lt is ~ le y x); totality is instead needed for the density/order-reflection substance, so the generalization still stands.
